## Major Rivers By Measured Length [...] Rivers are ranked by measured length from source to mouth, with the Nile and Amazon closely matched at the top.
 The Amazon's massive discharge and the Yangtze's economic importance complement their length rankings.
 Rivers in North America and Asia support major transportation corridors and energy production.
 Accurate length data benefit from modern satellite mapping and consistent methodology across studies. [...] Length estimates for major rivers depend on identifying the furthest source tributary and the main outflow point. The Nile traditionally leads on this basis, fed by tributaries from Lake Victoria and highland regions in Ethiopia.

The Amazon challenges the Nile with comparable length, carrying the world's largest discharge by volume. Its complex network of tributaries in the Amazon basin makes precise measurement a topic of ongoing study and debate.

results.title: How Long Is the Nile River? Exact Length, Facts & Full Guide
results.content:
The Nile River is about 6,650 kilometers (4,130 miles) long, which makes it traditionally known as the longest river in the world. It flows from the heart of East Africa all the way to the Mediterranean Sea, crossing deserts, forests, and ancient lands along its path. For thousands of years, the Nile’s length and constant flow have played a vital role in making it a lifeline for millions of people. [...] The Nile River length reaches about 6,650 kilometers (around 4,130 miles).
 The river, through its flow, passes by 11 countries and connects diverse cultures and landscapes.
 It takes nearly three months for the Nile’s water to travel from the main source to the mouth at the Mediterranean Sea.
 The river has two basic tributaries: the White Nile and the Blue Nile; they both meet in Sudan. [...] The Nile River stretches for about 6,650 kilometers (around 4,130 miles), which makes it one of the longest rivers in the whole world.
 The Nile flows north through 11 countries until it finally empties into the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt.
 Some researchers and scientists think that the Amazon River might be slightly longer, so the debate still goes on.
 Measuring the Nile isn’t easy, as its length depends on how scholars define its starting point and which tributaries are included.

## From Quarks to Quasars's post

### From Quarks to Quasars

14 December 2025  ·

The world’s longest rivers, ranked by length.

The Nile or the Amazon? Scientists still can’t agree.

For over a century, the Nile –stretching 4,132 miles (6,650 km) from Uganda to Egypt – held the title of Earth’s longest river. But recent Brazilian and Peruvian surveys suggest the Amazon may edge it out, clocking in at up to 4,345 miles (6,992 km) when traced to its furthest Andean source.

### How long is the Nile River?

The Nile River is approximately 4,100 miles long and was historically thought to be the longest river in the world. There is plenty of debate surrounding this, however, for many believe the Amazon River in South America might be longer. According to the United States Geological Survey, the Nile is about 100 miles longer than the Amazon.
